body.p: Applicant has reviewed the Office action dated February 12, 2024, and the references cited therein. Claims 1-13 and 16 are currently pending. Claim 16 is withdrawn from consideration. Claims 1-13 stand rejected. Claims 14-15 are canceled. Claim 16 is withdrawn from examination.
Applicant's Amendments

Applicant, in view of the current rejection over the combined teachings of the Mahajan and now-cited Mesin references, has amended independent claim 1 to expressly state that the claimed wearable device is configured for performing electromyography of a thoracic diaphragm.
In particular, Applicant's claim 1 now recites:
A wearable device for monitoring one or more vital signs of a human
body, the wearable device comprising:
a carrier configured to fit, while in use, fully around the human body, at an
abdominal part thereof; and
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes

including one or more first electrode and one or more second electrode, wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are arranged on the carrier to be brought in contact with a skin of the body in use, and wherein all electrodes of the plurality of conductive electrodes are configured for operating simultaneously to receive
electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling monitoring of a membrane
potential of one or more muscles in the body,
wherein the wearable device is configured for performing
electromyography of a thoracic diaphragm,
wherein the one or more first electrode is arranged on the carrier to be in
contact with a side part of a torso of the body near the thoracic diaphragm, the one
or more first electrode being configured to cooperatively receive a first electrical signal indicative of the membrane potential of the thoracic diaphragm of the body
and for providing the first electrical signal as a measurement signal;
wherein each electrode of the one or more second electrode and the one or
more first electrode is arranged aligned on the belt, such that the one or more
second electrode is aligned with the one or more first electrode, the at least one
second electrode thereby being arranged for receiving a second electrical signal
indicative of one or more further electric physiologic signals from the body,
wherein the second electrical signal in particular is indicative of a further
membrane potential, and
wherein the one or more second electrode is arranged for providing the
second electrical signal separate from the first electrical signal, the second electrode thereby providing a filter signal, for enabling filtering of the first
electrical signal using the second electrical signal for enabling electromyography
of the thoracic diaphragm. (Emphasis added).
Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the grounds for rejection of the

previously pending claims in view of Applicant's further amendments to the claims and remarks addressing the shortcomings of the prior art with regard to particular recited elements of the claimed invention.
Please charge any fee deficiencies to Deposit Account No. 12-1216. Grounds for Rejecting the Claims

1. Claims 1-5 and 11 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being obvious over Mahajan, WO 2015175904 (Mahajan) in view of Mesin (NPL; Separation of propagating and nonpropagating components in surface EMG).
2. Claim 6 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Mahajan and Mesin and in view of McGrane, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0019988 (McGrane).
3. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Mahajan and Mesin and in view of Maesani, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0273590 (Maesani).
4. Claims 8 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over
Mahajan in view of Mesin and Maesani as applied to claim 7 and in further view of Muccio, U.S. Pub. No. 2012/0016440 (Muccio).
5. Claim 9 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Mahajan and Mesin in view of Hsiao, U.S. Pub. No. 2012/0265025 (Hsiao).
6. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Mahajan and Mesin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Sims, U.S. Pub. No. 2007/0293781 (Sims).
7. Claim 13 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Mahajan and
Mesin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Tupin, U.S. Pub. No. 2011/0060215 (Tupin).

Applicant, in view of at least the current further amendments to claim 1, traverses the grounds for each and every rejection for at least the reasons set forth herein below. Applicant addresses the specific rejections in the order they arise in the Office Action.
Applicant's Specific Responses to the Grounds for Rejection
1. Rejection of Claims 1-5 and 11 as being obvious over Mahajan in view of Mesin
Applicant, in view of the current further amendments to independent claim 1, traverses

the rejection of claims 1-5 and 11, as being obvious over the combined teachings of Mahajan and Mesin. A proper case of obviousness cannot be established with regard to any one of the currently pending claims since the teachings of the cited Mahajan and Mesin references cannot be combined in a manner that results in Applicant's currently claimed invention.

Moreover, a proper reason cannot be established for one skilled in the art to modify Mahajan's teachings, in view of Mesin, in a way that would result in Applicant's claimed invention. Notably, none of the references cited in the Office action demonstrates any awareness of a particularized problem that would provide a reason to modify Mahajan (in view of Mesin) in a way that resulted in Applicant's claimed invention.
a. Applicant's Claimed Invention
Applicant's claimed invention is directed to a wearable device including a particular

electrode arrangement that facilitates carrying out electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm of a wearer of the wearable device. In particular currently amended claim 1, provided in clean form below, recites:
A wearable device for monitoring one or more vital signs of a human
body, the wearable device comprising:
a carrier configured to fit, while in use, fully around the human body, at an
abdominal part thereof; and
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes

including one or more first electrode and one or more second electrode, wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are arranged on the carrier to be brought in contact with a skin of the body in use, and wherein all electrodes of the plurality of conductive electrodes are configured for operating simultaneously to receive
electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling monitoring of a membrane
potential of one or more muscles in the body,
wherein the wearable device is configured for performing
electromyography of a thoracic diaphragm,
wherein the one or more first electrode is arranged on the carrier to be in
contact with a side part of a torso of the body near the thoracic diaphragm, the one
or more first electrode being configured to cooperatively receive a first electrical
signal indicative of a membrane potential of a thoracic diaphragm of the body and
for providing the first electrical signal as a measurement signal;
wherein each electrode of the one or more second electrode and the one or
more first electrode is arranged aligned on the belt, such that the one or more
second electrode is aligned with the one or more first electrode, the at least one
second electrode thereby being arranged for receiving a second electrical signal
indicative of one or more further electric physiologic signals from the body,
wherein the second electrical signal in particular is indicative of a further
membrane potential, and
wherein the one or more second electrode is arranged for providing the
second electrical signal separate from the first electrical signal, the second electrode thereby providing a filter signal, for enabling filtering of the first
electrical signal using the second electrical signal for enabling electromyography
of the thoracic diaphragm. (Emphasis added).

Thus, Applicant's claimed invention, as presented in further-clarified independent claim 1, recites a wearable device that is particularly configured for performing electromyography of a thoracic diaphragm of a wearer. Specifically, the wearable device includes first and second conductive electrodes that, while obtaining different signals, are nevertheless configured to operate substantially the same way by "operating simultaneously to receive electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling monitoring of a membrane potential of one or more muscles in the body." (Emphasis added). Consequently, the signals provided by the first conductive electrode and the second conductive electrode are directly comparable to each other. As such, the first electrical signal obtained from the one or more first electrode can be directly and straightforwardly filtered by the second electrical signal from the one or more second conductive electrode. The resulting filtered signal is a very weak diaphragmatic signal that (as a result of the filtering provided by comparing the two signals) nevertheless is measurable.

Applicant's disclosed/claimed invention thus addresses an underlying problem of EMG signals of the thoracic diaphragm being very difficult to obtain because of the many sources of noise (heart, organs, other muscles, etc.) proximate the signal source. Moreover, the disclosed/claimed invention is based on an insight that the shape of the thoracic diaphragm can

be used to the benefit of improving measurability and accuracy of EMG measurements of diaphragmatic movement. See Applicant's FIGs. 2A, 2B and 2C; and corresponding written description at page 12, line 22 to page 13, line 12.

Importantly, contrary to Applicant's disclosed/claimed invention, Mahajan does not describe obtaining a thoracic diaphragmatic EMG signal. The Office action's continued rejection of Applicant's claimed invention is based upon an erroneous interpretation of the type of monitoring to which Mahajan's teachings are directed. In particular, Mahajan's teachings are not directed to a wearable device configured for performing electromyography of a thoracic diaphragm.
b. The cited references do not, in combination, render Applicant's claimed invention
Applicant, at least in view of the current further clarifying amendment to independent claim 1 discussed herein above, traverses the rejection of independent claim 1.

Mahajan, upon which the current rejection of independent claim 1 primarily relies, describes a device that does not obtain a diaphragmatic EMG signal. Rather, Mahajan describes measurement of thoracic motion and thoracic volume which, according to paragraph [0070], relates to a thoracic and diaphragmatic breathing profile. Paragraph [0070] explains that the diaphragmatic breathing profile is determined using thoracic and diaphragmatic expansion sensors.

Mahajan in paragraph [0070] refers to "diaphragmatic expansion sensors" that perform a "measurement of strain." Such strain measurements enable sensing diaphragmatic expansion by "measurement of changes in girth or displacement of the upper and lower abdomen." Mahajan, indeed, mentions EMG sensors. However Mahajan describes using the EMG sensors to measure organ function drive. See Mahajan, at paragraph [0074]. None of the paragraphs cited in the Office action [0063], [0070] and [0074] describes using the EMG sensors to provide a diaphragmatic EMG signal output measurement.
On the other hand, the teachings of paragraph [0070] are consistent with the following additional instances of "strain sensor" teachings of Mahajan at:
Q paragraph [0013]: "a thoracic motion sensor";
Q paragraph [0016] which states that "chest wall and thoracic volume
monitoring [are sensed] using distributed displacement sensors",
Q paragraph [0017]: "measurement of thoracic motion and thoracic volume and
lung mechanical response through broadband acoustic methods"
Q paragraph [0033] which states that "[a]n array of displacement sensors 18
may also be included to measure displacement e.g. of the thoracic cavity."
Q paragraph [0034]: "thoracic motion array 72";
Q paragraph [0075]: "thoracic expansion detection";
Q paragraph [0087]: "measurement of thoracic motion and thoracic volume and
lung mechanical response" (which relates to par. [0017]);
Q paragraph [00113]: "motion sensors"
Q paragraphs [00102] and [00120]: "thoracic motion and thoracic volume".

Applicant adds that claim 1 was previously clarified to recite a combination of features that unequivocally describe Applicant's claimed invention as having first and second conductive electrodes that are of a same type/physical alignment such that both are configured for providing comparable membrane potential signals to facilitate providing the claimed thoracic diaphragmatic EMG signal output measurement.

Mahajan, for a different purpose and unrelated to measuring any thoracic activity, indeed describes EMG sensors at multiple instances. However, none of the instances concerns/suggests using the EMG sensors to measure an EMG of the thoracic diaphragm of a wearer of a wearable device. Moreover, Mahajan never mentions any EMG sensor that directly measures a "membrane potential of the thoracic diaphragm" as an electrical signal, in order to perform "electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm" in accordance with Applicant's claimed invention.

The Office action, at pages 4 and 5, at several occasions observes that paragraphs [0070], [0030] and [0087] disclose multiple sensors that can measure thoracic activity, and asserts that Mahajan thereby anticipates the measuring of "membrane potential of the thoracic diaphragm" as an electrical signal. However, such assertion does not properly follow from the noted paragraphs' teachings.

Applicant's claimed structural arrangement facilitates making a direct measurement of a membrane potential of the thoracic diaphragm, which enables performing EMG of the thoracic diaphragm. In particular, such direct measurement is made possible us of the signals of the

"second electrodes" to filter the majority of signals of the "first electrodes" to yield the very weak electrical diaphragmatic signals. Thus, Applicant's claimed invention is based on an insight (not mentioned in the cited references) that the shape of the thoracic diaphragm can be used to the benefit of improving measurability and accuracy of EMG measurements on the diaphragmatic movement. See Applicant's FIGs. 2a-c and corresponding description at page 12, line 22 to page 13, line 12.
It follows that the Office action's reasoning regarding Applicant's claimed "filter signal" is also erroneous.

Moreover, Mahajan's FIG. 1 (showing sensors on a belt), does not disclose Applicant's claimed first and second type electrodes being "aligned on the belt" as in claim 1. The belt in Mahajan appears to be broad and at best the sensors 16 are aligned, but not with respect to other sensors.

The above shortcomings in Mahajan are not addressed/remedied by the teaching of the cited Mesin reference, upon which the Office action relies to fill certain admitted shortcomings in the teachings of Mahajan. Mesin appears to present a comprehensive study on a technique for separating propagating and non-propagating components in surface Electromyography (EMG) signals. Mesin describes using an adaptive filter to estimate delays between signals at different channels and to separate the two components. See Mesin, Abstract.
Mesin presents an analysis of surface EMG signals for the purpose of separating

propagating and non-propagating signal components, without reference to respiratory functions or the (thoracic diaphragm) muscles involved in breathing. Mesin does not mention "diaphragm," "thoracic diaphragm," "breathing" or "vital signs", and therefore cannot be reasonably deemed to be directed to Applicant's claimed wearable device that is configured for performing electromyography of a thoracic diaphragm.

The Office action refers to an example in Mesin that allegedly describes an EMG device that has a three-electrode array for gathering electrode signals, wherein the electrode signals are processed in order to acquire an accurate EMG signal of a target muscle. This is done in order to test and validate the proposed method for separating the propagating and non-propagating components (e.g. see Mesin, page 131, section 2.5).

However, given Mahajan's failure to describe the measurement of a membrane potential of the diaphragm in order to perform EMG thereof, the teachings of Mesin cannot be properly applied to Mahajan's disclosure in a way that results in Applicant's claimed invention since the teachings of Mahajan and Mesin are not compatible in as much as Mahajan's disclosure is directed to detecting thoracic motion and expansion using displacement sensors. See Mahajan, at paragraphs [0016], [0033] and [0070]. In contrast, Mesin describes detecting EMG signals, but does not describe how such EMG signal detection teachings of Mesin could be incorporated into Mahajan's disclosure to render Applicant's currently clarified invention wherein the wearable device is configured for performing electromyography of a thoracic diaphragm.
For at least the above-provided reasons, Applicant's claimed invention recited in
currently amended independent claim 1 is not rendered obvious by the combined teachings of Mahajan and Mesin.
